Chainalysis vs TRM Labs vs Elliptic vs Cognyte: Crypto Analytics Compared
Compare four crypto analytics platforms for wallet screening, transaction monitoring, sanctions, investigations and forensics.
Reviewed and updated by FluidRWA · October 2, 2026
Chainalysis vs TRM Labs vs Elliptic vs Cognyte: Crypto Analytics Compared editorial infrastructure visual
Short answer

Chainalysis is a strong starting point for mature KYT and investigation programs; TRM Labs for configurable monitoring, threat intelligence and case workflows; Elliptic for institutional wallet screening and transaction monitoring; and Cognyte for intelligence-led law-enforcement investigations that combine blockchain tracing with broader investigative analytics. The four products should not be treated as interchangeable.

Start with the decision your team has to make

If your product receives deposits, you may need a wallet risk check before crediting a customer. If an alert fires, an analyst needs a case record they can explain and revisit. A public-sector investigation has a different task: connecting blockchain activity to other evidence. Those jobs call for different demonstrations from vendors.

Chainalysis, TRM Labs and Elliptic are relevant to private-sector screening and monitoring. Cognyte is more closely associated with intelligence-led investigations. Ask each company to demonstrate the decision your team makes, the data behind it and the record you can export afterward.

What to Ask Each Provider to Show

Chainalysis sells blockchain intelligence, KYT and investigation products to compliance teams and investigators. In a demonstration, separate the screening decision from the analyst's later investigation; they are different jobs.

Its KYT product focuses on monitoring incoming and outgoing crypto transactions, risk scoring, alerts, behavioral rules, case management and API integration. Chainalysis also has investigation tooling and data products that can support deeper forensic work.
Ask Chainalysis to demonstrate these requirements if they matter to your team:
KYT and transaction monitoring
investigator workflows
exposure analysis across many networks and tokens
API-connected deposit and withdrawal controls
case management and escalation evidence

The main diligence question is whether Chainalysis' depth, pricing and operating model fit the buyer's actual risk volume. A smaller tokenization platform may not need the same tooling footprint as a global exchange.

TRM Labs is often evaluated for transaction monitoring, wallet screening, investigations, fraud detection and threat intelligence. It is relevant where compliance teams want flexible alerting and case management around deposits, withdrawals, wallets, counterparties and behavioral patterns.
Ask TRM to demonstrate these requirements if they matter to your team:
configurable transaction monitoring rules
wallet and counterparty screening
threat intelligence and illicit-finance typologies
collaborative alert review
API integration into internal compliance workflows
fraud, sanctions and investigation support
public-sector or enterprise-grade investigative context

The main diligence question is how well TRM's risk categories, attribution and workflows match the buyer's product. For example, a stablecoin payout business may care more about corridor-specific withdrawal checks, while a tokenized fund may care more about investor wallet allowlisting and sanctions changes over time.

Elliptic is frequently evaluated for wallet screening, transaction monitoring, risk scoring and investigation workflows. Its materials emphasize real-time monitoring, configurable risk rules, automatic rescreening, wallet context and support for financial institutions, regulators, law enforcement and crypto businesses.
Ask Elliptic to demonstrate these requirements if they matter to your team:
wallet screening before allowing transactions
ongoing transaction monitoring
automatic rescreening of prior activity
entity context for reducing false positives
investigation tools for escalated cases
risk scoring across blockchain networks
compliance evidence for regulated teams
The main diligence question is whether Elliptic's coverage, risk methodology and alert workflow align with the buyer's compliance policy and operational staffing.
Cognyte

Cognyte positions BLINK around blockchain investigations for law-enforcement and intelligence teams. Its public materials emphasize following transaction trails, identifying suspects, generating investigative leads and combining blockchain activity with complementary analytics.
Ask Cognyte to demonstrate these requirements if they matter to your team:
intelligence-led cryptocurrency investigations
suspect and entity identification across crypto services
historical and ongoing transaction tracing
lead generation connected to broader investigative data
public-sector confiscation or organized-crime workflows

The main diligence question is whether the buyer needs an investigative intelligence platform or an operational compliance product embedded in customer onboarding, deposits and withdrawals. Those are different systems, evidence models and procurement processes.

How Tokenization Teams Should Use These Tools
A tokenized asset project should not wait until after launch to think about blockchain analytics. The monitoring design should be part of the operating model.
Important decision points include:
investor wallet screening before allowlisting
subscription and redemption monitoring
stablecoin payment screening
reserve wallet monitoring
sanctions rescreening after onboarding
transfer restrictions for permissioned tokens
escalation rules for suspicious activity
evidence retained for auditors, banks and regulators

If a tokenization platform allows transfers only between approved wallets, blockchain analytics can help determine whether a wallet should be approved, monitored, paused or removed from the allowlist.
Buyer Checklist
Before choosing Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic, Cognyte or another analytics provider, ask:
Which chains, tokens and stablecoins are fully supported?
Are indirect exposures measured, and how many hops matter for our policy?
Can alerts be tuned by asset, corridor, amount, user type and risk category?
Does the API support pre-transaction checks?
Can the provider monitor both deposits and withdrawals?
How are false positives handled?
Can cases be exported for audit or regulatory review?
Does the provider support automatic rescreening?
Who owns policy decisions after an alert is generated?
How does the provider integrate with KYC, custody, tokenization and payment systems?
Practical Recommendation
Shortlist providers based on the compliance decision you need to automate.
Choose Chainalysis if your priority is mature KYT, investigation depth and institutional recognition.
Choose TRM Labs if your priority is flexible rules, threat intelligence and operational monitoring.
Choose Elliptic if your priority is wallet screening, ongoing transaction monitoring and institutional crypto risk workflows.
Consider Cognyte when the primary requirement is intelligence-led public-sector investigation rather than customer-level transaction monitoring.
Then test all three against your real wallet flows. The best provider is the one that gives your compliance team accurate, usable signals without creating an unmanageable alert queue.

FAQ
Which is better: Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic or Cognyte?

There is no universal winner. Chainalysis, TRM Labs and Elliptic are natural candidates for private-sector crypto compliance and investigation workflows. Cognyte is more specifically positioned around intelligence-led and law-enforcement investigations. Buyers should shortlist by operating workflow rather than brand recognition.
Do tokenization projects need blockchain analytics?

Tokenization projects need blockchain analytics if investors, issuers, wallets, stablecoin payments, redemptions or transfers touch public blockchain addresses. Private or fully permissioned workflows may still need monitoring if assets bridge to public networks.
Is KYT the same as KYC?
No. KYC verifies the person or business. KYT monitors what crypto funds and wallets are doing onchain. Many regulated tokenization workflows need both.
What should buyers test before choosing a blockchain analytics provider?

Test chain coverage, wallet attribution, alert quality, false positives, sanctions screening, case management, API reliability, Travel Rule connections, reporting evidence and support for the exact assets used in the product.
Can blockchain analytics tools stop risky transfers automatically?
Some products can support pre-transaction screening and API-based policy actions, but implementation depends on the buyer's wallet, custody, token contract and operations design.
Do these providers replace legal advice?
No. They provide data, monitoring and case-management workflows. Legal obligations, licensing and policy decisions still require legal and compliance review.
What is most important for stablecoin products?

Stablecoin products should check supported chains, stablecoin asset coverage, source and destination risk, sanctions exposure, redemption controls and whether alert workflows can be connected to payment operations.
